## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4925db94254c845cf7164baef7cccc0280b62ab6`
Local-runs: probe — `node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --self-test`, run in a throwaway worktree of the head (`/tmp/claude-0/seat3/wt-31289`, since removed) and of `origin/main` (`b3bd75d8`, also removed), because the brief asks for the before and after counts and for diffs of the printed brief and template (exit 0 both; 368 cases on main, 373 at the head). In the same worktrees I also ran `--template` and `--brief-template`, bare and with `--face` schema, rules, narrowing and declaration (20 outputs, all exit 0, diffed pairwise); a scratch copy of the script with one added print, to read each changed battery's case count against its floor; `node scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` (exit 0, every file at its ceiling, headroom 0); `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 31289` (exit 3, GOVERNED, Tier S); `node scripts/check-commit-card-trailers.mjs --range origin/main..HEAD` (exit 0); `node scripts/pm/check-skill-id-lint.mjs` (exit 0); and the self-tests of `check-governed-queue-guard` (403 cases), `check-owed-reviews` (84), `check-half-states` and `post-stamped`, which import this module (all exit 0). Bytes per edited line were taken with `wc -c`.
Scope: the 4 `hits` of `git diff origin/main...refs/seat3/pr-31289` (merge base `07559ce5`): .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/coordinator.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/dispatch-runbook.md + the one file in the diff that implements them: scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs (the brief, the template, their jsdoc and self-tests). The diff has no remainder. Under main's rule the `+` half is "the files those hunks make a claim about", which is the same file here, so the scope is the same under main and under the PR. `07559ce5..origin/main` is 2 commits (`2f369cd3a`, `b3bd75d81`); neither touches these files or the queue guard. Code read, not reviewed: scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs (carry and record legs), `regenCarry` / `isOutsideReviewSurface` / `REVIEW_SURFACE_EXCLUDED_PROSE_FACES` in record-recognisers.mjs, scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs, and the rule text in references/execution-duties.md L100-L135, lanes/skills.md, lanes/review.md, platform-readings.md L385, triage-duties.md L12 and AGENTS.md (the governed-surface paragraph and the self-test section). Rulings 6203713500 and 6442046166 were read on GitHub.

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #31179 (body; triage 6710244771; claim 6713507940), the PR body (the live body equals /mnt/project-files/card-31179/body-v1.md apart from one trailing blank line), the report /mnt/project-files/card-31179/report-v1.md, the order /mnt/project-files/skills-seat3/order-31179.md, the single commit `4925db94` and the net diff. The seat's mid-flight rulings (1)-(3) are taken as given. Rules are judged under main as it stands. Where the PR's own new rules would change a judgment, I say so.

- **Item 1, the at-tier scope.** Implemented as ordered.
  - contract-review.md L14-L15: the scope is `hits` plus the files in the diff that directly implement or enforce them. Those files are judged against the contract. Code outside the diff is read only. `Scope:` lists both halves. "Never narrower than `hits`" stays.
  - L39 (the ④ line): "被引代码读而不审" becomes "实现文件审合契约、diff 外只读". This is the order's wording.
  - The brief (hits faces) says the same, names the remainder as the order does (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets), and says the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`. The ④ judge line adds "For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence?"
  - The template notes say the same. The record body of the template is byte-identical to main (`Scope: PATH-ONE, PATH-TWO + CITED-FILE`).
  - Nothing goes beyond the order. On paper the at-tier scope does not shrink. Main already gave the remainder to the lane seat at `TIER_DEFAULT`, and main only read the claimed files. The PR now reviews the implementing files in the diff, which is more than main asked.
- **Item 2, the re-review trigger.** Implemented as ordered.
  - L40-L41: every finding is graded must-fix, should-fix or nit. Nit means "无碍正确性与契约" (no effect on correctness or the contract). Only the first two grades earn a delta review by the same reviewer. A nit-only round is final.
  - The brief's ④ line carries the third grade and the delta rule. The template's ④ note asks for the grades.
  - Main's L42 read "只落发现的 commit 由同一复核者 delta 复核;无 must-fix 即止". Read literally, a should-fix-only round was final on main. Under the PR, a should-fix earns a delta. So the PR is stricter than main for should-fix and equal for nits. It is never looser.
- **Item 2, the head-move constraint.** Solved without a guard change. The guard confirms the claim.
  - L41 limits what happens to a nit: it is an accepted deviation, it moves to a follow-up card, or it is fixed only on the prose faces.
  - `regenCarry` carries a record over a hop only when every moved path is a prose face (`.changeset/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `content/docs/`, `apps/docs/`, through `isOutsideReviewSurface`), carries `merge=os-regen`, or came from the base. Any other path is refused, and the reason names it ("neither a pure regeneration nor a prose-only move"). The guard is not in the diff.
  - So a nit fixed in code moves the head. Under L40 the new head then owes a full round, and L49 still governs the head move. That is more review, not less.
  - The seat reads this in contract-review.md. A card thread does not read it: see S4.
- **Item 3, adoption.** Implemented, with gaps in how the seat checks and records it (S2, S3, S5).
  - New L46: when a card thread's isolated sub-agent posts a record "照上" (per the lines above) on the current head, the dispatching seat checks `Scope:` and the independence pair, adopts the record, and reviews only what it leaves out.
  - "照上" brings in the order's conditions by reference: the full record shape (L33-L36, the `--template` command at L35), a brief from `--brief-template` (L43), and a reviewer who is not the drafter and was not fed the drafter's conclusions (L45). The current head is stated in the line. The `Scope:` check is stated.
  - L32 changes "席内与子代理同形" to "席内与各子代理同形" and pays with "恒不算" → "不算" (net 0 bytes). "dev 自评" still does not count, so a thread's self-review stays out. The meaning is kept.
  - SKILL.md L190 becomes 「受管/spec 面欠 ①–④,席只达档补审现 head 记录未盖处。」 (115 bytes, one line, ruling 1).
  - dispatch-runbook.md L137: the seat keeps "复核采纳或补缺" in place of "契约复核".
  - coordinator.md 〈四〉: "线程复核落 PR,席采纳或补缺" is added. It does not name `--brief-template` or isolation, which the order's edit list asked for (S4).
- **The thread's deviation (SKILL.md L190).** It holds.
  - 「席起隔离达档审」 would make an at-tier seat start an isolated sub-agent. That contradicts contract-review.md L20-L21 ("达档者席内审", "派发席席内达档审").
  - The dropped condition "seat not at tier ⇒ isolated sub-agent" is still stated in two places a seat reads: execution-duties.md L119 (「余面未达档 ⛔ 不自审,起隔离子代理」; executing seats read it every fire, per SKILL.md's stage index) and platform-readings.md L385 (「不达档起隔离达档子代理或等档」).
- **Ruling (3), execution-duties.md L119.** No contradiction.
  - Adopting a record is not a self-review. When a gap is left, a seat below tier still must not review it itself and must start an isolated sub-agent. L119 says exactly that, and L46 does not override it.
  - When nothing is left, nothing is owed. L119 is not an order to start a sub-agent when no review is owed.
  - A literal reader could still see a conflict with L21 or L119 and, under SKILL.md L44 (two rules conflict ⇒ act on the stricter), re-run the covered scope. That costs tokens but never lowers review (N1).
- **Ruling (2), the deleted ① ② ③ lines.** Each fact has a home and can be reached from it.
  - At the head `--brief-template` prints, for every face (default, schema, rules, narrowing, declaration): "① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.", "② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line." and "③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated." These are the deleted L37-L38 facts, word for word in English. `--template` prints the three headings.
  - L43 points every brief at `--brief-template`, and L33 keeps "①②③逐项".
  - A seat reviewing in-seat reads `--template`, whose notes carry the headings but not the meanings (N4).
- **Item 4, policy text.** SKILL.md carries one clause (adoption). The scope and re-review detail lives only in contract-review.md (ruling 1).
- **Who reads each new line.**
  - SKILL.md L190: the seat at ACCEPT.
  - contract-review.md L14-L15, L39-L41 and L46: the seat or reviewer running or adopting the review.
  - dispatch-runbook.md L137: the seat and the thread splitting the work.
  - coordinator.md 〈四〉: the coordinator opening a thread, and the seat asking for one.
  - Every new line has a named reader. Not every line says enough for that reader (S4).
- **Item 4 of the check, old-rule sweep.** I grepped `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` for: 无 must-fix 即止, 读而不审, 所断言, 一并读, read as one, make a claim about, 全量复核, whole-PR review, 起隔离, 隔离子代理, 席内达档, and delta.
  - None of the old rule survives. "Tier H 人批与队列守卫仍整张 PR" (L16) is about landing, not review scope. lanes/review.md L15 and triage-duties.md L12 give the delta to the original reviewer, which still holds. AGENTS.md's Tier S paragraph needs a current-head `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS record and does not say who renders it, so it still holds.
  - In the code, "make a claim about" now appears only on the narrowing face, and a pin enforces that.
- **Item 3 of the check, the narrowing face.**
  - `--brief-template --face narrowing` and `--face declaration` print byte-identical output at the head and on main (cmp). Neither ruling's words change.
  - The narrowing and declaration TEMPLATES do change, because the notes are shared. Three changes print on the narrowing template: the new Scope note, one added narrowing clause, and the sentence "Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit". This makes the narrowing face disagree with itself (S1).
- **Item 5, code.**
  - The brief and template edits do what the rule says. The narrowing brief branch is untouched.
  - No reader parses `Scope:` or the grade labels. `scopeLineOf` exists only in the self-test. No script outside the module imports `contractReviewBriefLines`, `contractReviewTemplateLines`, `contractReviewRecordLines` or `RECORD_SCOPE_PLACEHOLDERS`. The record body is unchanged.
  - Records written to the old template and to the new one parse the same way. The queue guard's 403-case self-test, which drives this module, passes.
  - New self-test pins cover the new branches:
    - the scope lines and the named remainder (letter-C battery);
    - the nit grade and the delta rule, and the implementing-file ④ line (brief battery);
    - the narrowing brief kept as ruled;
    - the template notes' implementing files and grades (template battery).
    - Four old pins were rewritten to the new words.
  - Floors follow AGENTS.md (names pinned, one floor per battery). Measured counts against floors:
    - template 32/30 at the head (31/29 on main);
    - brief 23/21 (20/18);
    - letter C 19/19 (18/18).
    - Each floor rose by exactly the cases added, so the slack is unchanged.
  - The self-test reads contract-review.md for the claim, hold and handoff lines. None of those lines moved.
- **Item 6, budgets.** Within budget.
  - The repo's ratchet is `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`: line count per file plus widest table row. It exits 0 with every file at its ceiling.
  - Line counts are unchanged: SKILL.md 319, contract-review.md 60, coordinator.md 49, dispatch-runbook.md 245. The ratchet script is not in the diff, so no ceiling moved.
  - Every added .md line is 106-120 bytes. The new adoption line, L46, is exactly 120. The only line over 120 in the three reference files is L22, the verbatim handoff template, which is unchanged from main.
  - record-recognisers.mjs grows 3356 → 3383 lines. It has no ceiling.
- **Item 7, process.** Checked.
  - Labels: documentation, size/m, skip-changeset. The PR is a draft, has no assignees, and is authored by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
  - The body has: `Fixes #31179`, the order quoted verbatim and untranslated (with the coordinator's proposal and the owner's 「同意立卡」 and 「通知席位并立skills卡」), the six 维护者速读 lines, `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` at line start, a before/after table, the narrowing answer, the item-2 solution, and the self-test counts.
  - The model waiver ("this card ran on the project's default model") names no model.
  - The only model words are inside the two verbatim quotes. These are the owner's message and the coordinator's proposal that the owner approved. I judge that acceptable: SKILL.md L98 says ruling quotes are copied untranslated, and the card body carries the same quotes. The body says the quotes are the only place a tier is named another way.
  - No model id appears in the rule text, the code or the commit. `check-commit-card-trailers` exits 0.
  - Exactly the five files are touched (`changed_files` 5).
  - Tier: `check-governed-merges --pr 31289` exits 3: GOVERNED, Tier S, `.claude/**` ×4; record-recognisers.mjs is off the register; size +72 / −45.
  - Check-runs read 2026-11-07T22:39Z: 24 success, 20 skipped, 1 in progress, 0 failures.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right. `.claude/**` and `scripts/pm/**` are repo tooling and publish nothing. No published accept set or platform behaviour moves, so `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Claim.** All five paths are inside claim 6713507940. The queue guard, the ratchet scripts and execution-duties.md are untouched, as ruled. No breach.
- **Tier.** GOVERNED, Tier S. Under main's rules the owning seat may land it through the queue once a current-head `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS record is on the PR or card and every check is green. The body's 「需要你做的」 says this and leaves the landing call to a maintainer.
- **This PR is reviewed under the rules it changes.** This record was run by an isolated reviewer briefed by the seat, which satisfies both main and the PR. Under main, my should-fix findings end the round, because main's L42 stops when there is no must-fix. Under the PR's own L40-L41, a fix of any should-fix below earns a delta review by the same reviewer, and the nits do not.
- **Landing note (item 8).**
  - Mechanically, nothing loosens. The queue guard is unchanged and still refuses a Tier S diff without a current-head at-tier PASS record. A nit fixed in code voids the record, as before.
  - On paper, the scope and delta rules are equal to main or stricter.
  - The one real loosening is reviewer independence under adoption. On main, the dispatching seat briefed the at-tier reviewer (L45 "喂入同上"). Under L46, the drafting thread now briefs its own isolated sub-agent, and the seat checks only `Scope:` and the independence pair. It does not check the brief, and nothing in the record shows what the reviewer was fed (S3). The order asked for this trade.
  - The owner's words on their face: the owner asked a question, then answered the coordinator's three-point proposal with 「同意立卡」 (agree to file a card) and 「通知席位并立skills卡」 (tell the seats and file a skills card). That approves the content of the proposal as a card. It is not a word on the exact rule text, or on landing a change to the review rules. Main's rules need no human word for Tier S. But the card itself leaves the call open, and this PR changes the review that gates its own landing. So I agree with putting the landing to a maintainer, as the seat plans.
- **Other sites (not in the diff, nothing owed).**
  - execution-duties.md L119 and platform-readings.md L385 still hold.
  - lanes/skills.md L12 ("契约复核归派发席席内") still holds: the seat still owns the review and adopts or fills it.
  - The coordinator's standing instruction to card threads lives outside the repo. The card says the coordinator updates it.

### ④ Design judgment

- **should-fix S1: the narrowing face now has two grading scales.**
  - The rule (L40) grades every finding three ways, on every face.
  - The narrowing brief keeps "name each finding must-fix or should-fix". A new pin enforces "no nit" there.
  - The narrowing TEMPLATE prints the shared ④ note "Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit" just before its narrowing sentences.
  - So a narrowing reviewer reads two scales. Neither ruling fixes the number of grades: 6442046166 letter A hangs ④ on the face, and 6203713500 letter B makes it a face at tier. The PR read "do not change the narrowing face" more widely than the rulings go.
  - The effect is stricter, never looser: a nit-less reviewer turns every finding into a delta. That is why this is not a must-fix.
  - The 速读 line 「收窄面…一字未动」 holds for the brief, not for the narrowing template.
  - Fix: either give the narrowing brief the nit grade (a code line, no ratchet), or say in L40 that the narrowing face keeps two grades and keep the shared note off that face. Put the choice to the seat.
- **should-fix S2: L46 does not say how the gap review is recorded.**
  - The template says "the NEWEST one naming this head governs". L15 says `Scope:` is "⛔ 不窄于 `hits`".
  - A seat that posts a record covering only the gap therefore replaces the thread's record with one whose `Scope:` is below the floor.
  - The template's `Reviewed-by` note ("the session that RENDERS or ADOPTS") allows one correct reading: the seat posts one record whose `Scope:` names the full floor plus the gap it reviewed, and states which part it adopted. But no line says so.
  - The ACCEPT pointer (SKILL.md L190) also does not say it names the adopted record's id.
  - Fix: in contract-review.md (paying by deletion), say that the seat's gap record restates the full `Scope:`, names the adopted record's comment id, and signs `Reviewed-by:` as the adopter. Or say that with no gap, the ACCEPT pointer names the adopted record.
- **should-fix S3: one adoption condition cannot be checked.**
  - The order says the record counts only if its brief came from `--brief-template`, fed the card, the PR and the check-runs, and not the drafter's conclusions.
  - L46 brings this in through "照上", but tells the seat to check only `Scope:` and the independence pair. The record does not carry its brief, and the drafter writes it.
  - On main, the seat wrote the brief itself, so the question did not arise.
  - The pair is also weak evidence here. By L44 a sub-agent record names the adopting seat in `Reviewed-by:`, so the seat checks a line that names itself. `Implemented-by:` names the thread's branch. Neither shows the reviewer was isolated from the drafter.
  - Fix: have the thread post the filled brief (or link it) beside the record, and have the seat read it before adopting. L46's "核 `Scope:` 与独立性对" would become "核简报、`Scope:` 与独立性对".
- **should-fix S4: the thread side of adoption and of nits is not written where a thread or the coordinator reads it.**
  - The order's edit list asks coordinator.md 〈四〉 and dispatch-runbook.md to say that the card thread's at-tier review is the `--brief-template` record posted on the PR.
  - coordinator.md says only "线程复核落 PR". That reads as any thread review, including the self-review that L32 refuses.
  - The runbook's thread half is unchanged.
  - The brief tells the sub-agent "nits alone end the round", but not the L41 rule that a nit is fixed only on prose faces or left. A thread that fixes a nit in code moves the head and voids the record.
  - Both failures are safe (the seat re-reviews), but they waste the tokens the order set out to save.
  - Fix: in coordinator.md 〈四〉, point to contract-review.md's adoption line or name the isolated `--brief-template` record, within its 120 bytes. In the brief, add after "nits alone end the round": "a nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up". The brief is code, not ratcheted.
- **should-fix S5: L46 does not say that `Scope:` must cover the floor before adoption.**
  - The order says the record counts "when … its `Scope:` line covers the floor".
  - L46 says "核 `Scope:` … 采纳,只补未盖处". That covers the case where the record does not reach the floor (the seat fills the gap). It does not say that a record whose `Scope:` is below `hits` breaks L15 and is not adoptable as the head's record.
  - This is low risk, because L15 already applies to every record. It is still worth one clause, folded into the S2 fix.
- **nit N1: L21 ("派发席席内达档审") and execution-duties.md L119 still read as unconditional.** A seat applying SKILL.md L44 (stricter rule wins) may re-run the covered scope. This never lowers review. Optional: "派发席席内达档审(采纳见下)".
- **nit N2: layout of the printed notes.**
  - In the template, the Scope note has one line about 115 characters long ("freely, ⛔ never below `hits`. The rest …"), and the ④ note has a short line ("On the narrowing face, with no `hits`, the narrowing").
  - The brief's ④ scope rule now breaks after "ONLY:".
  - One jsdoc line in `contractReviewBriefLines` runs past 130 characters.
  - These are cosmetic.
- **nit N3: the `Scope:` placeholder still reads `CITED-FILE`.** The notes now call that slot the implementing files. Keeping the placeholder keeps every reader and fixture stable (the thread's deviation 4), so this is fine. A later rename would be clearer.
- **nit N4: the meanings of ①-③ now reach an in-seat reviewer only through L43's pointer to the brief.** `--template`'s notes carry the headings only. Ruling (2) accepts this. A one-line note in the template ("① ② ③ as `--brief-template` states them") would close the gap at no ratchet cost.

Verdict: PASS

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: the coordinator's delta request with the thread's claims, body v2 (/mnt/project-files/card-31179/body-v2.md; the live body equals it plus a trailing signature line), the delta commit and its diff, and the first-round record.

- **S1, one grade scale.** Fixed.
  - The narrowing brief now ends with the shared `BRIEF_GRADE_LINES` in place of "name each finding must-fix or should-fix. A must-fix is a FAIL.".
  - Main against head on the narrowing brief, only two places differ:
    - the two lines of grading sentence, which become "Read the spec and the cited code in the live tree, and try to break the design." plus the five grade lines;
    - the shared two-line preamble outside the copy fence (see S3).
  - Every ruled sentence is byte-identical to main: the whole-diff floor paragraph, "the narrowing itself, read against the published spec on `main`", "declared capability away at the consumer", "the spec's own refusal real" and "⛔ never narrowed at the consumer".
  - The narrowing template's ④ note already said three grades, so template and brief now agree.
  - A pin enforces both the ruled sentences and the shared lines.
  - The 速读 and the narrowing section of the body now say this accurately.
